title: Spaghetti Carbonara
description: The real Roman carbonara — no cream, no shortcuts. Guanciale rendered slow, eggs tempered off heat, Pecorino folded in to form a glossy, black-peppered silk.
ingredients: Plenty of freshly cracked black pepper
instructions: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a rolling boil.

Cut guanciale into lardons about 1cm thick. Start in a cold pan over medium-low heat so the fat renders slowly — about 8 minutes — until crispy at the edges but still chewy inside. Remove from heat; keep warm.
In a bowl, whisk eggs, yolks, and three-quarters of the cheese. Season aggressively with black pepper.
Cook spaghetti until 90 seconds shy of al dente. Reserve 1 full cup of starchy pasta water before draining.
Add drained pasta to the guanciale pan off the heat. Toss to coat every strand in the rendered fat.
Pour the egg mixture over the pasta, tossing constantly. Add pasta water a splash at a time, tossing until a glossy, creamy sauce coats the pasta without scrambling. Work quickly.
Serve immediately on warm plates. Top with remaining cheese and a final crack of pepper.
notes: Off-heat is non-negotiable. The residual heat of the pasta finishes the eggs gently. If your sauce tightens up, a splash more pasta water loosens it instantly.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Char-edged chicken tikka folded into a silky tomato-cream masala built on toasted whole spices. The kind of dish that fills the kitchen with warmth before you've even sat down.
ingredients: 700g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 4cm pieces
For marinade: 180g full-fat yogurt, 2 tsp garam masala, 1½ tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp vegetable oil
For masala: 3 tbsp ghee, 1 large white onion finely diced, 6 garlic cloves minced, 25g fresh ginger grated
2 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp coriander seeds (toasted and ground)
1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp garam masala, 1½ tsp Kashmiri chili powder
instructions: Mix all marinade ingredients with the chicken. Cover and refrigerate minimum 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Broil or grill chicken on highest setting until deeply charred in spots — 8–10 minutes per side. Set aside. Don't crowd the pan.
Melt ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter 30 seconds.
Add onion with a pinch of salt. Cook 12–15 minutes stirring often until deeply golden — don't rush this.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add ground spices. Cook 1 minute, stirring, until the mixture smells toasty and darkens slightly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook uncovered 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oil separates and sauce is thick and deep red.
Add charred chicken pieces. Stir to coat. Pour in cream. Simmer 8 minutes.
Adjust salt. Finish with torn cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili gives the color without excessive heat. The char on the chicken is flavor — don't skip the broil step.

title: Baja Fish Tacos
description: Crispy beer-battered cod in warm corn tortillas with crunchy cabbage slaw, pickled jalapeños, and a smoky chipotle crema. Best eaten standing at the kitchen counter.
ingredients: 600g cod or mahi-mahi fillets, cut into 8cm strips
For batter: 150g all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp salt, 240ml cold lager beer
For slaw: 200g shredded green cabbage, 1 lime juiced, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, pinch sugar, salt
For chipotle crema: 150g Mexican crema or sour cream, 2 chipotle peppers in adobo (minced), 1 garlic clove (grated), lime juice
Pickled jalapeños, lime wedges, and fresh cilantro to serve
instructions: Toss cabbage with lime juice, vinegar, sugar, and salt. Let sit 20 minutes; it will soften and brighten.
Whisk crema ingredients together. Season with salt and lime. Refrigerate.
Whisk flour, baking powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt. Pour in cold beer and stir until just combined — lumps are fine. Batter should coat a spoon.
Heat 4cm of oil in a heavy pot to 190°C (375°F).
Pat fish dry. Dip in batter, let excess drip off, and lower carefully into oil. Fry in batches — don't crowd — 3 minutes per side until deeply golden. Drain on a rack.
Warm tortillas directly on a gas flame or dry skillet until charred in spots.
Build each taco: slaw, fish, chipotle crema, pickled jalapeños, cilantro. Squeeze lime over everything.
notes: Cold beer = crispier batter. The batter goes in the cold fridge while oil heats. Don't overcrowd the pot or the temperature drops and you get soggy fish.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached directly in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce. One pan, twenty minutes, and you have something that feels celebratory for a Tuesday morning.
ingredients: 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp smoked paprika, ½ tsp caraway seeds
Pinch of cayenne or Aleppo pepper
Fresh parsley and crusty bread to serve
instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide, heavy skillet over medium heat. Add onion and pepper with a pinch of salt. Cook 8 minutes until very soft.
Add garlic and all spices. Cook 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in tomatoes and sugar. Stir and simmer 10 minutes until sauce is thick and deeply flavored. Taste and season.
Use a spoon to make wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover the pan and cook 5–8 minutes until whites are just set but yolks are still runny. Check frequently.
Scatter crumbled feta over the top. Finish with parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.
Serve directly from the pan with bread for dipping.
notes: The difference between a perfect shakshuka and an overcooked one is about 2 minutes. Pull it when the whites look barely set — residual heat finishes them.

title: Classic French Omelette
description: The French omelette is a technique benchmark disguised as breakfast. Pale yellow, creamy inside, folds without a seam. Three eggs, two minutes, and your full attention.
ingredients: Optional fillings: fresh herbs, Gruyère, goat cheese
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl. Beat vigorously with a fork until completely uniform — no streaks of white. Season with salt and white pepper.
Heat a 20cm non-stick pan over high heat. Add butter. When it foams and the foam just begins to subside (don't let it brown), pour in the eggs.
Immediately stir with a fork using quick small circles while shaking the pan back and forth. Keep everything moving for about 30 seconds.
When the eggs are still slightly liquid on top (creamy, not set), stop stirring. Add any filling down the center.
Tilt the pan 45 degrees. Use the fork to fold the top third of the omelette over the filling.
Roll the omelette out onto a warm plate — the bottom fold completes itself as it tips over the pan edge. The seam should be on the bottom.
The omelette should be pale yellow with no browning.
notes: Everything happens in under 3 minutes. Have the plate warm, your filling ready, and your full attention on the pan. Practice makes perfect — this is worth making ten times.

title: Miso Ramen
description: A rich, deeply savory miso tare stirred into a dashi-and-pork broth, with wavy ramen noodles, a soft egg, corn, and crispy chili-sesame garlic oil pooled on top.
ingredients: For tare: 80g white miso, 2 tbsp sake, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame paste
For broth: 1L dashi (or light chicken stock), 500ml pork or chicken stock, 2 tsp toasted sesame oil
1 tbsp gochujang or chili bean paste
Toppings: corn kernels, scallion, nori, toasted sesame seeds, bamboo shoots
Chili oil or sesame oil to finish
instructions: Soft-boil eggs: 7 minutes in boiling water, ice bath immediately, peel and marinate in 2:1 soy-mirin for at least 1 hour.
Whisk all tare ingredients together until smooth. Set aside.
Brown ground pork in a dry pan over high heat, breaking it up, until crispy in spots. Add gochujang, garlic, and ginger. Cook 2 more minutes. Set aside.
Bring dashi and pork stock to a gentle simmer. Keep hot.
Cook noodles according to package. Drain; divide between 2 bowls.
Add 3 tablespoons of tare to each bowl. Ladle hot broth over to fill — stir to dissolve the tare.
Top with pork, halved egg, corn, bamboo shoots, and scallion. Drizzle with chili oil and sesame oil.
notes: The tare is the soul of the bowl — make extra and keep it in the fridge for a week. The broth should be hot when it hits the tare, not simmering in it.
